candidate1/02026-08-28When technicals and fundamentals are directionally aligned but supporting data (volume, positioning) is ambiguous, a one-third trim is a proportionate calibrated response to near-term mean-reversion risk — it captures the expected fade without overcommitting to a thesis the data quality doesn't fully support. The hard trailing stop on the residual is the correct structural fix for the "no defined exit" asymmetry rather than a reason to increase the trim size; here the stop never activated and the trim itself delivered the edge. The firm should resist both the "trim more to compensate for residual risk" impulse and the "trim less because the stop covers it" impulse — they solve different problems and the correct trim size should be set on signal conviction alone.

candidate1/02026-08-28Trimming near a 52-week high on capex/valuation grounds captures the "trend intact but drifts down modestly" regime — the stock can fall 3–5% without breaking structure, which is exactly the gap between "trend says hold" and "asymmetry says trim." The key is that the trim's expected-value edge and the hard stop's tail-risk capping are independent protections: the trim was what made this trade right here, but the stop is what prevents the rare capex-miss gap from turning a modest trim into a still-large loss on the residual.
